zhen: quick follow-up to the gateway/edge retry convo. I sketched a tiny contract for resume-checkpoints, trailer auth, and billing interactions. main goals: avoid edge buffering, make resume deterministic, and prevent double-billing.

olivia: love this. can you paste the headers and a short state-machine?

zhen: sure. headers i propose:
``
Idempotency-Key: <uuid>
X-RW-Resume-Token: <opaque; checkpoint-id|offset|sig>
X-RW-Final-Code: ok|retryable|fatal|partial
X-RW-Checkpoint-Seq: <int>
X-RW-Cacheable-Prefix: yes|no
```
Edge rules (short):
- if connection dies before trailer -> network error -> edge may attempt retry only if Idempotency-Key present or resume-token previously observed.
- if trailer includes X-RW-Final-Code=fatal -> no retry.
- if trailer includes X-RW-Resume-Token -> edge may present that to client for resume; edge should not replay upstream unless Idempotency-Key present.
- checkpoint seq increments monotonically; resume-token ties to seq.

raj: question: how big are resume tokens? we should keep them small (opaque sig + seq). upstream should be able to reconstruct state from token without heavy memory.

marco: agree. also: what about side-effecting streams (eg append logs)? we only allow resume if upstream guarantees at-least-once-idempotent-apply from token; otherwise require full-replay with Idempotency-Key.

emily: billing angle: billing-bot suggests we store a per-Idempotency-Key ledger with fields: billed_tokens_committed, billed_tokens_pending. On final ok, commit pending -> billed. On retry with same Idempotency-Key, reference same ledger. On resume-token resume, bill only delta tokens delivered to client.

billing-bot: ledger: created ledger_id=ldb-3311 for idempotency-key present. pending=0. :moneybag:

zhen: good. a few more behavioral details:
- Edge should expose checkpoint events to long-lived clients (websocket/sse) so clients can persist latest resume-token locally and reconnect without asking edge to buffer.
- For short HTTP streaming clients, edge returns last-observed resume-token in trailers when available.
- Cache semantics: only allow prefix caching if X-RW-Cacheable-Prefix=yes AND final-code ok OR resume-token present and prefix stable. Edge must validate token seq before committing cache.

olivia: what about auth/trailers? we should require trailer authenticity: trailers must be delivered over the same TLS conn and upstream must sign resume-tokens (HMAC with upstream key) so edge can verify origin. add a short security note to RFC.

raj: nit: define maximum checkpoint frequency to avoid token spam (eg min 200ms or min 32 tokens), upstream-configurable.

marco: ops note: rollout plan - gated canary with `edge.resume.stateless=true` off by default. add config `edge.resume.max-buffer-bytes` to protect memory if teams enable buffering.

zhen: testing ideas: 1) upstream shim that emits tokens every 1s and on chunk boundary; 2) failure tests where client disconnects after token T and reconnects asking resume from T+1; 3) double-bill attempt if idempotency missing.

emily: +1 on tests. i'll add billing integration tests for token-deltas and idempotency replay dedupe.

olivia: ok i will draft the RFC patch: include header defs, state machine (short), security note (token signing + TLS), and rollout checklist (canary flags + metrics to watch: resume-success-rate, replay-rate, billing-discrepancies).

raj: thumbs up. if we want, we can add a small diagram for client-edge-upstream handshake in the doc.

marco: one more thought: for long resumable sessions, include a TTL for resume-tokens (eg 24h) and a soft-expiry that forces full replay or Idempotency-Key check. protects storage and billing windows.

zhen: agreed. i'll add TTL to token spec. thanks all. i'll push the upstream shim WIP to my branch and link when ready.

olivia: great thread. i'll wait for PR and we can canary next week. :shipit:
